text:
maria: FYI customer 'AtlasPay' escalated — noticing p95/p99 regressions since ~09:20 UTC, major spike in user-facing latency and a support ticket claiming timeouts. stack: hosted API, model gpt-neoX-20b-quant.
jamal: grabbing traces now. any associated errors in logs? request IDs?
maria: attached in ticket: reqs 8362a/8362b, top symptoms: p95 ~ 680ms -> 1.6s, p99 up to 3s. no 5xxs reported, just long tail of token generation stalls.
lin: I see one of our dashboards — sudden jump in kv_cache.miss_rate and kv_cache.evictions at 09:18. looks like a high-cardinality key burst. putting graphs: PromQL snippet below.
lin: ```promql
sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[1m])) by (shard)
/ sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[1m])) by (shard)
``` 
lin: miss_ratio jumped from 5% -> 62% on most inference shards in region us-west-2. evictions/sec doubled.
olivia: customer claims this correlates with a product release that starts attaching an SDK session ID header to each request (X-Client-Session). could be high cardinality keys created by our prefix-key generator including session id.
kevin: quick note — recent SDK 1.3.0 added session identifiers as part of metadata to help telemetry. that ended up in the request metadata block we use to compute prefix cache keys. oops.
maria: so root cause hypothesis: ephemeral session IDs are inflating prefix cardinality -> cache warmup churn -> evictions -> misses -> higher latency.
jamal: makes sense. reproducing locally is straightforward. repro steps:
jamal: ```bash
# emulate many short-lived session ids
for i in {1..8000}; do
  SID=$(head -c8 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'a-zA-Z0-9' | head -c8)
  curl -s -H "X-Client-Session: $SID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate > /dev/null &
done
wait
```
jamal: you'll see backend kv miss rate spike and p99 climb.
lin: confirmed in a canary: when session id included in prefix, the prefix-cardinality metric skyrockets and hotset fracturing causes hot keys to be evicted before warmup completes. essentially warmup/eviction loop.
olivia: immediate mitigations we can push:
olivia: 1) short-term config change: enable prefix_normalization strip_headers=["X-Client-Session"] on the public API gateway for affected routes. this removes ephemeral header from cache key construction. low-risk rollback.
olivia: 2) increase prefix cache capacity for us-west-2 by 20% for the next 2 hours while we roll fix.
maria: customer wants timeframe — can we get a quick patch today?
kevin: SDK patch ready to stop sending session id in metadata for cacheable calls. we can ship a minor release but customers may still be on older SDKs.
jamal: operational hotfix plan:
jamal: - deploy prefix_normalization to prod gateway (target 09:55)
jamal: - bump cache capacity (09:58)
jamal: - monitor kv_cache.miss_rate, p95/p99 for 10m windows
jamal: - if no improvement, run emergency rollback to previous routing (but expecting fix will help)
lin: longer-term fixes:
lin: - canonicalize cache key generation: drop ephemeral fields by default and provide explicit allowlist for cacheable metadata
lin: - implement session-id fingerprinting: if header present, hash to a low-entropy bucket (N-way sharding) to avoid full-cardinality expansion
lin: - adopt segmented-LRU to reduce single-key eviction thrash for hot prefixes
olivia: additionally propose 'drip warmup' where we limit concurrent warmup inflight per-shard and backoff when eviction pressure high. this avoids overshooting cache work during bursts.
maria: can you paste quick dashboard alerts we should use to auto-detect next time?
lin: suggest:
lin: ```yaml
alerts:
  - name: KV Prefix Miss Surge
    expr: increase(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]) > 1000 and (kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.2)
    for: 5m
  - name: KV Eviction Storm
    expr: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (region) > 500
    for: 3m
``` 
kevin: added a note in SDK repo to revert session header usage for non-diagnostic paths and will open a PR for a runtime opt-out flag.
maria: timeline update — prefix_normalization deployed at 09:56, capacity bump applied at 09:59.
incidents-bot: Deployment to gateway/prefix-normalize completed (deployed by jamal) :rocket:
maria: initial post-fix: p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 480ms within 6m, p99 down to ~750ms. kv miss rate down to ~8%.
olivia: leaving this open for 24h monitoring and a follow-up RFC for canonicalization + segmented-LRU.
jamal: will follow up with runbook changes for caching best-practices and a short KB for customer support to call out SDK headers as a common pitfall.
maria: thanks team :pray: please add any follow-ups to the ticket and CC the customer success lead.
kevin: opening SDK PR and email to partners to warn about session-id opt-in.
lin: I'll schedule a deeper postmortem if p95 climbs again. :eyes:
